info.bio: Músico de rock y de blues. Nació en Clarksdale, Mississippi en 1931. Músico autodidacta, comienza muy joven con el grupo Kings of Rhythm, y de disk-jockey en la radio. En 1951 graba su primer éxito "Rocket 88" (algunos críticos dicen que esta canción fue el primer Rock and Roll de la historia). En 1956 tocando en St. Louis, una joven llamada Annie Bullock salta al escenario y se pone a tocar con ellos= nace Tina Turner. Cosechan sus mejores éxitos en los 60, compartiendo giras con los Rolling Stones.

scenes.name: Rock'n'roll
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: Fusión de rhythm'n'blues y country, con mucho más peso del primero. Chuck Berry inventa en 1955 el rock'n'roll tal como se conocerá durante cincuenta años (la guitarra como instrumento protagonista, canciones propias que hablan a los adolescentes); Bo Diddley aporta el ritmo «hambone», Little Richard y Esquerita el histerismo y el maquillaje (el primer «decadence-rock»), Jerry Lee Lewis el piano feroz y Sun Records el rockabilly. Elvis Presley es, para Scaruffi, «la primera gran estafa del rock'n'roll». Buddy Holly y Eddie Cochran abren otra vía; en paralelo nacen el soul (Ray Charles), la exótica (Martin Denny, Esquivel), la música electrónica de cinta y, en Gran Bretaña, el skiffle.

podcast.title: "Spoken Ike Vocals" on "It's Gonna Work Out Fine"
podcast.body: For Ike & Tina Turner's hit "It's Gonna Work Out Fine," Mickey Baker performed the "spoken Ike vocals" on the record, which Ike Turner would then perform live. "Sylvia played the lead guitar part while Mickey did the spoken Ag vocals, which Ag would do live."

podcast.title: Control over Tina Turner's Career
podcast.body: Ike Turner, Tina Turner's abusive, controlling, and drug-addicted husband, held complete decision-making power over her musical career until she left him in 1975. This included the decision to record her first solo album, "Tina Turns the Country On!," as a country record to expand her audience. "Ike he made the decisions about her musical career."

podcast.title: Danger Mouse Production Commitment
podcast.body: Danger Mouse was initially unavailable to produce The Black Keys' *Attack & Release* album because he had committed to producing an album for Ike Turner. However, the project ultimately fell through, making Danger Mouse available for The Black Keys. "Unfortunately, he was unavailable because he was committed to producing an album for Ike Turner."

"doing the same kind of things that Ike Turner had been doing for chess and modern."

podcast.title: Vocals on Rocket 88
podcast.body: Ike Turner provided vocals on Jackie Brenston's "Rocket 88" in the early 1950s. This song was considered an early, "frightening" example of rock and roll, blending rhythm and blues with hillbilly and country music. "This is Jackie Brinston's Rocket 88 with Ike Turnway vocals."

xref.body: Danger Mouse's prior commitment to producing an album for Ike Turner initially prevented him from working with The Black Keys on *Attack and Release*. However, the eventual collapse of the Ike Turner project freed him up to collaborate with the band. "Unfortunately, he was unavailable because he was committed to producing an album for Ike Turner."

xref.title: Producer Collaboration with Black Keys
xref.body: Danger Mouse became The Black Keys' first external producer for their fifth album, *Attack and Release*, playing keyboards and bass on the record. He was initially unavailable due to a commitment to produce for Ike Turner, but that project's cancellation made him accessible. He later produced one song on *Brothers* and then fully produced and co-wrote all 11 tracks on *El Camino*. "Danger Mouse played a bunch of different instruments on the album, keyboards and bass mainly, and a few other musicians were called into filling with guitars and vocals and even clarinets."
